title: Gulf states come under Iranian fire as US strikes intensify
facts: Iran launched overnight missile and drone strikes targeting multiple countries across the Persian Gulf region.
Bahrain, Iraq, Kuwait, Oman, Qatar, Jordan, and Syria took defensive action against incoming Iranian projectiles.
The Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps claimed responsibility for striking United States military assets in the region.
United States airstrikes hit civilian infrastructure in southern Iran including the Bandar-e Khamir bridge in Hormozgan province.
Iranian media reported that at least eight people were killed in overnight United States attacks on southern Iran.
Emergency sirens sounded and security threat levels were raised in Doha, Qatar, following loud explosions.
The Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps claimed to have struck the Al Udeid Air Base situated outside Doha.
The Qatari Ministry of Interior confirmed that a child was injured by falling shrapnel during the attack.
An Iranian strike damaged an electricity and water desalination facility in Kuwait, causing fires across power generation units.
Desalination plants supply approximately 90 percent of Kuwait's domestic water.
The Iranian military claimed it destroyed a United States air control radar in the northern Ghanim region of Oman.
Kurdish counterterrorism forces in northern Iraq reported that coalition forces downed eight explosive drones over Erbil.
The Jordanian military shot down three Iranian missiles that entered its national airspace.
Chinese Foreign Minister Wang Yi and Pakistani Foreign Minister Ishaq Dar called for an immediate regional ceasefire.
Iranian authorities stated that 38 people were killed and over 400 injured since bilateral talks began in Switzerland on June 22.
